Fam
FAM
noun (Millennial slang)
Clipped from family. In AAVE and hip-hop from the 1990s, fam meant close friends regarded as family; it also became central to London Multicultural English ("you get me, fam?"). In the 2010s it spread across Millennial and Gen Z speech as a term of address and affection for friends ("thanks, fam"), and the phrase "squad and fam" covered one’s inner circle.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Fam is family, extended to friends: the people close enough to be called kin. "Love you, fam." "What’s good, fam?" The Christian observation: the word reaches for something deeply biblical, and the gospel fulfils it. God builds families, "God setteth the solitary in families" (Psa 68:6), and the Church is a household where strangers become kin. "Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God" (Eph 2:19). The Lord Jesus redefined family around Himself: "For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother" (Mar 3:35). Believers are adopted children of one Father and call each other brother and sister, which is exactly what "fam" means. Paul tells Timothy to treat "the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity" (1Ti 5:2). The slang also shows a longing. Many young people use "fam" for friends because their own families are broken or absent, and the friends have had to stand in. That is a sorrow the Church should see and answer. A father loves his own family first, as Scripture commands, and also teaches his children to open their home and church to friends who need a fam, so that the word becomes true: brothers and sisters in Christ, sharing tables and burdens.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial slang (1990s AAVE and hip-hop; 2010s mainstream) clipped from family, for close friends as kin; redeemable, for the Church is the household of God (Eph 2:19) where those who do His will are brother and sister (Mar 3:35).

FAM, n. (AAVE and hip-hop, 1990s; Millennial and Gen Z slang, 2010s–present; clipped from family) Close friends regarded as family; used in address. "Thanks, fam."

Webster (1828), root family: FAMILY, noun [Latin familia.] 1. The collective body of persons who live in one house and under one head or manager; a household, including parents, children and servants, and as the case may be, lodgers or boarders. 2. Those who descend from one common progenitor; a tribe or race; kindred; lineage. Thus the Israelites were a branch of the family of Abraham; and the descendants of Reuben, of Manasseh, etc., were called their families. The whole human race are the family of Adam, the human family 3. Course of descent; […]

Decode for parents: when a friend calls your child "fam," ask whether that friend has a family; your table may be the answer.

Key Scripture

Psa 68:6 — "God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land."

Eph 2:19 — "Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;"

Mar 3:35 — "For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother."

1Ti 5:2 — "The elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity."

Gal 6:10 — "As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith."

Modern Corruption

Fam reaches for kinship among friends, often because families are broken; the gospel fulfils it in the household of God and calls Christian homes to take in the solitary.

expand to see more

If there is a corruption here, it is not in the word but in what it often replaces. Many young people call friends "fam" because their homes have failed them: absent fathers, divorce, distance. Friends become family by necessity. Sometimes the "fam" is a gang or a crew with its own loyalties and dangers. The longing is good; the substitutes can be fragile or worse.

The redemption is the Church as a real family and Christian homes as open doors. "As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith" (Gal 6:10). Teach the young to honour their own families, to be faithful friends, and to bring their friends into the household of God, where the word "fam" is literally true: one Father, one Lord, brothers and sisters for ever.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin familia (household) → family → 1990s AAVE / hip-hop fam → London MLE → 2010s Millennial and Gen Z address.
